# Data overview

Libraries and loading data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(ggstatsplot)
library(viridis)

reports <- read.csv("https://zenodo.org/records/10573715/files/CSE_student_performances%20%281%29.csv")
```

## Student Profile

Insert code interpretation here

```{r}

# creating variables
age_data <- reports %>%
  filter(!is.na(Age), !is.na(Gender))

age_min <- floor(min(age_data$Age))
age_max <- ceiling(max(age_data$Age))
bin_size <- 1

# groups shown in the dropdown
groups <- c("All students", unique(as.character(age_data$Gender)))

# Create one histogram trace per group
student_demo_plot <- plot_ly()

for (i in seq_along(groups)) {
  
  group_name <- groups[i]
  
  group_data <- if (group_name == "All students") {
    age_data
  } else {
    filter(age_data, as.character(Gender) == group_name)
  }

  student_demo_plot <- add_trace(
    student_demo_plot,
    data = group_data,
    x = ~Age,
    type = "histogram",
    name = group_name,
    visible = i == 1,
    opacity = 0.85,
    xbins = list(
      start = age_min,
      end = age_max + 1,
      size = bin_size
    ),
    marker = list(
      color = viridis(length(groups), option = "D")[i]
    ),
    hovertemplate = paste(
      "Age: %{x}",
      "<br>Students: %{y}",
      "<extra></extra>"
    )
  )
}

# Add dropdown buttons
visibility <- lapply(seq_along(groups), function(i) {
  as.list(seq_along(groups) == i)
})

dropdown_buttons <- lapply(seq_along(groups), function(i) {
  list(
    method = "update",
    args = list(
      list(visible = visibility[[i]]),
      list(title = paste("Age Distribution:", groups[i]))
    ),
    label = groups[i]
  )
})

student_demo_plot <- student_demo_plot %>%
  layout(
    title = "Age Distribution: All students",
    bargap = 0.2,
    margin = list(t = 100),
    template = "plotly_white",
    xaxis = list(title = "Age"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Number of students"),
    updatemenus = list(
      list(
        type = "dropdown",
        buttons = dropdown_buttons,
        x = 1,
        y = 1.18,
        xanchor = "right"
      )
    ),
    margin = list(t = 100)
  )

student_demo_plot

```

# Analysis 2 - Social Life

## Distribution of number of friends

\
*Insert written analysis here later*

```{r}
#summary of friends data 

friend_summary <- reports %>%
  summarise(
    total_students = n(),
    valid_responses = sum(!is.na(NumberOfFriend)),
    missing_responses = sum(is.na(NumberOfFriend)),
    missing_percent = 100 * mean(is.na(NumberOfFriend)),
    mean_friends = mean(NumberOfFriend, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_friends = sd(NumberOfFriend, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_friends = median(NumberOfFriend, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr_friends = IQR(NumberOfFriend, na.rm = TRUE),
    minimum_friends = min(NumberOfFriend, na.rm = TRUE),
    maximum_friends = max(NumberOfFriend, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  print()

#plotting of distribution of number of friends
gghistostats(
  data = reports,
  x = NumberOfFriend,
  xlab = "Number of friends",
  title = "How many friends do students have on average?",
  subtitle = "Distribution of number of friends",
  binwidth = 3,
  centrality.type = "mean",
  centrality.line.args = list(
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.8,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ),
  bin.args = list(
    fill = viridisLite::viridis(5)[3],
    color = "white"
  ),
  results.subtitle = FALSE,               
  ggtheme = ggplot2::theme_bw()        
)


```

How do these three variables (number of friends, likeness of public presentation, and likeness of new things) relate with one another?

*Insert written interpretation*

```{r}
#preparing data to be plotted (will update later)

plot_social_life_report <- reports %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(LikeNewThings, LikePresentation),
      ~ case_when(
        str_to_lower(str_trim(as.character(.x))) %in% c("yes", "1") ~ 1L,
        str_to_lower(str_trim(as.character(.x))) %in% c("no", "0") ~ 0L,
        TRUE ~ NA_integer_
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  drop_na(NumberOfFriend, LikeNewThings, LikePresentation) |>
  mutate(
    preference_group = str_c(
      "New things: ", if_else(LikeNewThings == 1, "Yes", "No"),
      "\nPresentations: ", if_else(LikePresentation == 1, "Yes", "No")
    )
  )

#testing boxplot 1

ggbetweenstats(
  data = plot_social_life_report,
  x = preference_group,
  y = NumberOfFriend,                                 
  plot.type = "box",
  results.subtitle = FALSE,
  pairwise.comparisons = FALSE,
  centrality.plotting = FALSE,
  xlab = "Preference combination",
  ylab = "Number of friends",
  title = "Number of friends by preferences",
  ggtheme = ggplot2::theme_bw()
)

```

```{r}
#testing 3d interactive plots  ???????????????????????????????????

set.seed(11)

plot_social_life_report %>%
  plot_ly(
    x = ~ jitter(LikeNewThings, amount = 0.06),
    y = ~ jitter(LikePresentation, amount = 0.06),
    z = ~ NumberOfFriend,
    color = ~ preference_group,
    colors = viridisLite::viridis(4),
    type = "scatter3d",
    mode = "markers",
    marker = list(size = 4, opacity = 0.7),
    text = ~ str_c(
      preference_group, "\nNumber of friends: ", NumberOfFriend
    ),
    hoverinfo = "text"
  ) %>%
  layout(
    title = "Number of friends by preferences",
    scene = list(
      xaxis = list(
        title = "Likes new things",
        tickvals = c(0, 1),
        ticktext = c("No", "Yes")
      ),
      yaxis = list(
        title = "Likes presentations",
        tickvals = c(0, 1),
        ticktext = c("No", "Yes")
      ),
      zaxis = list(title = "Number of friends")
    )
  )



```

Creating a new variable: Extroversion

*Insert reasoning here (cite?)*

```{r}
#use dplyr to create new variable (extroversion) based on other three

extroversion_reports <- reports %>%
  mutate(LikeNewThings = case_when(
    LikePresentation == "Yes" ~ 1L,          #make it so it's not duplicate code
    LikePresentation == "No"  ~ 0L,
    TRUE ~ NA_integer_)) %>%
  mutate(LikePresentation = case_when(
    LikePresentation == "Yes" ~ 1L,
    LikePresentation == "No"  ~ 0L,
    TRUE ~ NA_integer_)) %>%
  mutate(Extroversion = NumberOfFriend * 0.50 + 
           LikeNewThings * 0.25 +            #update math/percentages (add wieght?)
           LikePresentation * 0.25)
                                            #make a regression model?


#plot new variables distribution

gghistostats(
  data = extroversion_reports,
  x = Extroversion,
  xlab = "Extroversion rates",
  title = "How extroverted are students on average",
  subtitle = "Distribution of extroversion across students",
  binwidth = 2,
  results.subtitle = FALSE,             
  ggtheme = ggplot2::theme_bw() 
)
```
